subject: Integration runbook: SDK + auth patterns, routing & embeddings — post-demo follow-up
messages:

Subject: Integration runbook: SDK + auth patterns, routing & embeddings — post-demo follow-up

Hi Sasha / Alan —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps based on what we talked about (focus: how you’ll integrate Redwood into FinRail’s sandbox → prod flow):

What we agreed on
- Primary flows: user-facing chat + a backend enrichment pipeline that calls embeddings + a small reranker for statements flagged by fraud rules.
- Initial rollout: sandbox testing (api keys) -> staging (short-lived JWTs) -> prod (service accounts with KMS-backed signing).

Proposed technical runbook (high-level)
1) SDK onboarding: provide the language-specific quickstart (we attached the Redwood SDK setup PDF). Plan: SDK + minimal sample app that shows streaming + tool-calling + structured JSON output.
2) Auth patterns: recommend short-lived JWTs for server-to-Redwood calls (recommended rotation: 24h tokens signed by a KMS-managed key). API keys OK for sandbox/dev only.
3) Routing: use our route-by-policy header (region=us;tier=dedicated) for predictable latency. We'll provide an example middleware for your service mesh.
4) Embeddings & rerankers: we will ship a sample pipeline using our embeddings endpoint and an off-the-shelf dense-sparse reranker; metrics to capture: recall@K, latency P95.

Immediate asks from your side
- Confirm whether FinRail can accept a short-lived-JWT approach (we'll provide a sample token exchange flow).
- Share the IP allowlist for sandbox and the preferred SSO provider if you want RBAC on token issuance.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-setup.pdf (quickstart), finrail-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (draft MAP with milestones).

I'll loop Ben for the deeper auth/runbook details and Marissa for timelines and PoC metrics.

Cheers,
Karthik

Subject: Re: Integration runbook: SDK + auth patterns, routing & embeddings — post-demo follow-up

Thanks, Karthik — very helpful summary. A few clarifying questions from our infra team before we schedule the sandbox work: 

1) Service accounts vs API keys: for our compliance team, stateless API keys are discouraged in prod. You recommend JWTs signed by KMS — do you have a short example of the token exchange you mentioned (our token issuer is HashiCorp Vault backed)?

2) Rotation window: 24h tokens sounds good. Do you also support refresh tokens or an automated rotation endpoint? What's the recommended grace period for in-flight requests during rotation?

3) Rate limiting and burst: can Redwood route to a dedicated pool when we hit a threshold? We want to avoid tail-latency spikes during batch enrich jobs.

4) Embeddings model options: which models do you recommend for dense semantic search vs reranker input? We'd like to test both cheaper 8-bit quantized models and a higher-accuracy 16-bit variant.

5) Compliance / audit logs: what level of request metadata is available in Private deployment (we're planning to try Private if the PoC looks good).

If you can give short bullets and an example token exchange snippet (or a link), we can evaluate and get our infra folks on a 1-hour sandbox kickoff.

Best,
Sasha
Sasha Ivanov
Head of Platform Engineering | FinRail
sasha@finrail.com

Subject: Re: Integration runbook: SDK + auth patterns, routing & embeddings — post-demo follow-up

Hi Sasha — good questions, answers below (high-level + pointers).

1) Token exchange (Vault -> Redwood short-lived JWT) - Flow (simple):
   a) Vault issues a short-lived client credential to FinRail service identity (TTL ~1h).
   b) FinRail backend calls your token broker endpoint that exchanges the Vault credential for a Redwood short-lived JWT via our STS endpoint.
   c) Redwood validates the JWT signature against the KMS public key and issues a session token (24h) used for API calls.
   d) Example exchange snippet: https://drive.google.com/finrail/MAP (see section 2.1 exchange example).

Note: We support signed JWTs from customer KMS (you can upload the public key) or we can accept an OIDC id_token from your IdP and mint Redwood session tokens.

2) Rotation & grace period - Recommended: issue session tokens for 24h, rotate KMS signing keys every 30d. Grace strategy: accept previous-signing-key for a 5-minute window post-rotation for in-flight requests; for long-running streams we suggest re-auth at restart/checkpoint.

3) Routing & burst handling - Yes. Use header X-Redwood-Route: pool=dedicated;policy=burst-allow to route to your reserved pool. We also have a configurable throttle where we can shift lower-priority traffic to a cheaper model variant (auto-fallback). We'll add a middleware example in the SDK quickstart.

4) Embeddings & reranker guidance - For semantic search: start with the mid-tier 6B-quantized model for embeddings to reduce cost; compare against 13B 16-bit embeddings if you need recall lift. For reranking: use a small encoder-decoder reranker on top of dense results; we can ship a reference implementation using our /embeddings -> rerank pipeline. We'll include token-cost estimates in MAP.

5) Audit logs (Private)

Private deployments capture request-level metadata (timestamp, model_id, route, token_id, request_id, latency_ms) and retain logs per your retention policy. We can export to your S3/GCS or to an on-prem SIEM.

Next steps (proposed)
- Ben to share a short runbook draft with concrete curl/SDK examples and the revised MAP.
- FinRail infra: confirm Vault vs OIDC approach and preferred sample timeframe for the PoC (1–2 weeks).

Will follow up with the runbook attachment and a 60-minute sandbox kickoff slot — does Thursday morning PST work?

Thanks,
Karthik

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Integration runbook: SDK + auth patterns, routing & embeddings — post-demo follow-up

Hi Sasha — picking up the technical runbook items and attaching a trimmed MAP with concrete playbook steps. High-level implementation details below: 

Auth runbook (concise) - Phase A (sandbox): use static API keys scoped to sandbox project. No rotation required; keep keys in Vault and restrict by IP.
- Phase B (staging): implement Vault -> Redwood STS exchange. Sample curl:
  curl -X POST https://auth.redwood.dev/v1/exchange \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"assertion":"<vault-signed-credential>","aud":"redwood"}'
- Phase C (prod): service account flow: create service principal in your IAM, upload its public key to Redwood, and configure KMS signing. We recommend TTL=24h and a key-rotation cadence of 30d.

Rotation & streaming notes - For streaming sessions, include an auth-refresh checkpoint in the client that re-requests a fresh 24h session token if a stream is expected to run >20 minutes. Grace acceptance: 5 minutes post-key-rotation.

Routing & cost controls - We'll provide SDK middleware (node/python) that tags calls with route metadata and exposes a local in-memory batcher to keep latency predictable during bursts. For large backfills, use our batch ingestion API which is explicitly rate-limited and charged differently.

Embeddings/rerank sample config - Start: embeddings-6b-quant (cost-friendly) -> top-200 dense candidates -> rerank with small cross-encoder (13B-lite or 7B high-precision). We will include tuning scripts in the MAP.

Attachments: finrail-mutual-action-plan.xlsx (timeline + owner), redwood-sdk-setup.pdf (with middleware snippet).

I'll set up a Thursday 10am PST sandbox kickoff calendar invite after Sasha confirms — we can loop in your infra and security.

Best,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
